column5: decimal_separator is the only market format field with no fallback so a null value prints the literal text null inside every price
column6: formatCurrency at src/helpers/currency.ts merges the market rules over its defaults with const f = { ...DEFAULT_FORMAT - ...(format || {}) } and then reads each field. Every other field is defensive - thousand_separator falls back through separator || '' inside groupThousands - negative_format through (f.negative_format || '-{n}') - decimal_places through a typeof number guard - and symbol_position degrades safely because anything that is not the string after is treated as before. decimal_separator alone is interpolated raw into `${grouped}${f.decimal_separator}${decPart}` with no guard. A spread copies a key that is present with a null or undefined value and overwrites the default so a market whose format block carries decimal_separator: null produces the string 1234null50. Executed against the real function: a null yields $1234null50 and an explicit undefined yields $1234undefined50 while an omitted key correctly yields $1234.50. The MarketFormat interface at src/types/market.ts:2-10 declares every field optional so an absent value is expected by design.
column10: A market whose format block returns decimal_separator as null or as an explicitly present undefined rather than omitting the key. The panel controls this value per market.
column11: 1. Configure or mock a market format where decimal_separator is null. 2. Render any price through formatPrice from SettingsContext. 3. Read the output.
column12: The default separator is used whenever the market does not supply one - the same way every other field in the same function already degrades.
column13: The literal text null is printed between the whole and decimal parts of every price on the site.
column14: Every price - cart total - wallet balance and order amount in that market renders as unreadable text. It is a single misconfigured field away and affects the entire storefront at once rather than one screen.
column15: Guard the field like its siblings - use (f.decimal_separator || '.') at the interpolation - or filter null and undefined values out of the format object before the spread so a present-but-empty field cannot beat the default.

column5: An unparseable or missing amount is rendered as a genuine zero so a wallet balance that failed to load shows as no money
column6: formatCurrency at src/helpers/currency.ts coerces its input with const num = Number(amount) and then falls back with const safe = Number.isFinite(num) ? num : 0. Any value that is not a finite number - undefined - null - an empty string or a string that is already grouped such as 1234.50 with a separator - becomes 0 and is formatted as a real amount. Executed against the real function: an already grouped string returns $0.00 and a null returns $0.00. The reachable case is src/components/Cart/WalletCard.tsx:60 which renders wallet?.formatted_balance ?? formatPrice(userData?.wallet_balance) - so when the wallet payload is missing or the balance field is absent the customer is shown a formatted zero balance rather than a loading or error state. The server-formatted branch is correct - this is only about the client fallback.
column10: Wallet payload missing or its balance field absent - for example the wallet endpoint failing while userData is present from a cached session.
column11: 1. Load the wallet screen with the wallet endpoint failing so wallet is undefined and userData.wallet_balance is absent. 2. Read the available balance figure.
column12: A missing amount is distinguishable from a real zero - render a placeholder or the loading state rather than a formatted number.
column13: The balance renders as a fully formatted zero which is indistinguishable from an account that genuinely holds no money.
column14: A customer with money in their wallet is told the balance is zero when the fetch failed. That drives support contacts and can cause them to abandon a wallet-funded checkout. The same silent zero applies anywhere formatPrice receives a missing value.
column15: Return null or a placeholder from formatCurrency when the input is not finite and let the caller decide what to render - or keep the zero only for a genuine numeric zero and have WalletCard show its loading state while the wallet payload is absent.

column5: The recharge amount field strips the decimal point so a decimal entry is silently multiplied by one hundred
column6: handleAmountChange at src/components/Modals/DepositModal.tsx:39-47 sanitises the field with inputValue.replace(/\\D/g - '') which removes every non-digit character including the decimal separator - then parses the remaining digits with parseInt at :42 and writes the result back into the controlled input at :47. Typing 100.50 therefore leaves the digit run 10050 and the field becomes 10050 - one hundred times the intended amount. The separator is not rejected and no validation message is raised - the digits either side of it are simply joined. If whole-currency recharge is the intent then the correct behaviour is to reject or truncate the fractional part rather than concatenate it into the whole part.
column10: Any user typing or pasting a decimal amount into the wallet recharge field.
column11: 1. Open the wallet recharge modal. 2. Type 100.50 into the amount field. 3. Read the value the field now holds.
column12: Either the decimal is accepted as a fractional amount or the separator is rejected with a message - the digits after it are never promoted into the whole-currency part.
column13: The field silently becomes 10050 which is one hundred times the amount that was typed.
column14: A customer intending to add 100.50 is presented with a payment for 10050 in the market currency. The value is visible in the field so it can be caught - but the transformation is silent and the payment sheet that follows shows only the inflated figure.
column15: Sanitise to a single decimal-aware numeric pattern rather than stripping all non-digits - or if the recharge is deliberately whole-currency then truncate at the separator and surface a message explaining that fractional amounts are not accepted.

column5: The maximum recharge amount is a hard-coded number that ignores the market currency
column6: The deposit submit handler at src/components/Modals/DepositModal.tsx:84 rejects any amount above the literal 1000000 with the message from deposit.error.exceed. The limit is not read from settings and is not scaled by the active market currency - so the same numeric ceiling applies whether the market prices in a strong currency or one where a routine purchase already runs to six or seven figures. CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids hard-coding business values of this kind and section 7.4 requires monetary behaviour to follow the active market rather than a fixed constant. There is no matching minimum either - the only lower bound is the parsedAmount <= 0 check at :73 - so a recharge of the smallest possible unit is accepted while the ceiling is arbitrary.
column10: A market whose currency has a low unit value so that 1000000 units is an ordinary rather than an exceptional amount.
column11: 1. Switch to a market whose currency runs to large nominal figures. 2. Attempt a wallet recharge of an ordinary local amount above 1000000 units. 3. Observe the amount is rejected as exceeding the maximum.
column12: The recharge ceiling comes from settings and is expressed per market so it means the same thing in every currency.
column13: A single hard-coded ceiling applies to every market so it is far too low in some and far too permissive in others.
column14: Customers in high-nominal-value currencies cannot recharge ordinary amounts while customers in other markets face no meaningful ceiling at all. The limit also cannot be changed without a code release.
column15: Read the minimum and maximum recharge from the wallet or payment settings that SettingsContext already exposes and fall back to a documented default only when the setting is absent. Flag the need for the setting to the panel if it does not exist yet rather than adding another constant.
